```{r}
#| label: setup
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
here::i_am("manuscript/appendix.qmd")
root <- here::here()
source(file.path(root, "R", "piaac_prepare.R"))
source(file.path(root, "R", "estimators.R"))
source(file.path(root, "R", "country_summaries.R"))
source(file.path(root, "R", "figures.R"))
source(file.path(root, "R", "latex_tables.R"))
paper <- root
fig_dir <- file.path(root, "output", "figures")
latex <- knitr::is_latex_output()
options(piaac.stars = "ilr")
knitr::write_bib(c("base", "haven", "ggplot2", "patchwork", "knitr"), file = "packages.bib")

# Every number in this document is read from results written by the pipeline:
# R/03_estimate.R (results/, results_decile/) and R/04_mediation.R
# (results_mediation/, results_mediation_decile/). Nothing is typed in.
R <- function(f) readRDS(file.path(root, "results", paste0(f, ".rds")))
M <- function(f, dir = "results_mediation") readRDS(file.path(root, dir, paste0(f, ".rds")))
# Extended sample: earnings decile in 19 countries. Coefficients on the decile (1-10) are
# divided by 10, so that 100 x estimate is in percentile points of the national earnings
# distribution. Sorting results have tasks as the outcome and are not rescaled.
rescale10 <- function(x) lapply(x, function(d) { d$estimate <- d$estimate / 10; d$se <- d$se / 10; d })
RD <- function(f, rescale = TRUE) {
  x <- readRDS(file.path(root, "results_decile", paste0("art_", f, ".rds")))
  if (rescale) rescale10(x) else x
}
# Total and direct effects from mediate(), arranged as a specification sequence:
# "SKILL|M0" is the total effect and "SKILL|M4" the direct effect net of the 4 blocks.
med_seq <- function(ch) lapply(ch, function(r) do.call(rbind, lapply(c(total = "M0", direct = "M4"), function(m) {
  part <- names(which(c(total = "M0", direct = "M4") == m))
  x <- r[r$term %in% paste0("mean|", trait_names, "|", part), ]
  data.frame(term = paste0(sub("^mean\\|(\\w+)\\|.*$", "\\1", x$term), "|", m),
             estimate = x$estimate, se = x$se, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) })))
res <- list(
  ch = M("art_channels"), rho = M("art_rho"), sens = M("med_sens_grid"), ind = R("art_industry_split"),
  yard = R("art_yardstick"), rv1 = R("rv_full"),
  sc = R("art_skills_compl"), pc = R("art_pc_variants"),
  A = R("art_mp_A"), B = R("art_mp_B"), C = R("art_mp_C"), A0 = R("art_mp_nojob_A"), B0 = R("art_mp_nojob_B"),
  own = R("art_alloc_own"), job = R("art_alloc_job"), cell = R("art_alloc_cell"), tenure = R("art_alloc_tenure"),
  sup = M("art_channels_sup"), occ2 = M("art_channels_occ2"), broadA = M("art_channels_broadA"),
  m1 = R("m1"))
res$seq <- med_seq(res$ch)
res <- c(res, list(
  d_ch = rescale10(M("art_channels", "results_mediation_decile")),
  d_sc = RD("skills_compl"), d_pc = RD("pc_variants"),
  d_A = RD("mp_A"), d_B = RD("mp_B"), d_C = RD("mp_C"), d_A0 = RD("mp_nojob_A"), d_B0 = RD("mp_nojob_B"),
  d_own = RD("alloc_own", FALSE), d_cell = RD("alloc_cell", FALSE)))
res$d_seq <- med_seq(res$d_ch)
med_info <- M("run_info")
flow <- utils::read.csv(file.path(paper, "results", "sample_flow.csv"))
# Indirect effect through industry by sector, without the education industry and by country
# (replicate weights and plausible values). Decile results are in percentile points / 100.
dec10 <- function(x, pattern) lapply(x, function(d) { i <- grepl(pattern, d$term); d$estimate[i] <- d$estimate[i] / 10; d$se[i] <- d$se[i] / 10; d })
res <- c(res, list(
  e_all = R("art_effects_all"), e_noedu = R("art_effects_no_education"), e_sec = R("art_effects_sector"),
  e_occ = R("art_effects_occ"), e_occ2 = R("art_effects_occ2"), e_noteach = R("art_effects_occ2_noteach"),
  d_e_all = RD("effects_all"), d_e_noedu = RD("effects_no_education"), d_e_sec = RD("effects_sector"),
  d_e_occ = RD("effects_occ"), d_e_occ2 = RD("effects_occ2"), d_e_noteach = RD("effects_occ2_noteach"),
  d_ind = dec10(RD("industry_split", FALSE), "contrib$|^premium")))
if (is.null(res$ind)) res$ind <- R("art_industry_split")
gsize <- utils::read.csv(file.path(paper, "results", "group_sizes.csv"))
gsize_d <- utils::read.csv(file.path(paper, "results_decile", "group_sizes.csv"))
hom_edu <- utils::read.csv(file.path(paper, "results", "homogeneity_education.csv"))
hom_edu_d <- utils::read.csv(file.path(paper, "results_decile", "homogeneity_education.csv"))
hom_counts <- function(f) { h <- utils::read.csv(f)
  list(premium = h$rejected[h$quantity == "premium"], industries = seq_len(h$tested[1]),
       sorting = setNames(h$rejected[-1], sub("sorting[|]", "", h$quantity[-1]))) }
hc <- hom_counts(file.path(paper, "results", "homogeneity_industries.csv"))
hc_d <- hom_counts(file.path(paper, "results_decile", "homogeneity_industries.csv"))
descr <- utils::read.csv(file.path(paper, "results", "descriptives.csv"))
# Returns in separate samples (R/03_estimate.R) for Table A12; the linear interactions are res$sc.
# 12: deciles in the countries of the log-wage sample; 7: the countries that release deciles only.
res$ss <- R("art_split_samples"); res$d_ss <- RD("split_samples")
# Tertiary wage premium with and without the skills (R/03_estimate.R), Table A13.
res$er <- R("art_education_return"); res$d_er <- RD("education_return")
in12 <- names(res$ss); in7 <- setdiff(names(res$d_ss), in12)
res$d_ss12 <- res$d_ss[in12]; res$d_ss7 <- res$d_ss[in7]; res$d_sc12 <- res$d_sc[in12]; res$d_sc7 <- res$d_sc[in7]
countries <- names(res$seq)
K <- length(countries)
A_countries <- names(res$A)
countries_d <- names(res$d_seq)
K_d <- length(countries_d)
added_d <- setdiff(countries_d, countries)
N_d <- sum(utils::read.csv(file.path(paper, "results_decile", "countries.csv"))$n)
# Bridge between the outcomes: mediation estimates in the twelve countries with both.
bridge <- local({
  a <- unlist(lapply(countries, function(cc) res$ch[[cc]]$estimate))
  b <- unlist(lapply(countries, function(cc) res$d_ch[[cc]]$estimate[match(res$ch[[cc]]$term, res$d_ch[[cc]]$term)]))
  c(r = cor(a, b), slope = sum(a * b) / sum(a^2)) })
trait_names <- names(trait_label)

# Summary rows (countries and Mean) for one term, memoised.
.memo <- new.env()
S <- function(r, term) {
  key <- paste(r, term)
  if (is.null(.memo[[key]])) .memo[[key]] <- country_and_summary(res[[r]], term)
  .memo[[key]]
}
row_of <- function(r, term, stat = "Mean") { x <- S(r, term); x[x$country == stat, ] }
# Numbers for display, with a true minus sign (U+2212).
f <- function(x, d = 1) { x <- round(x, d); x[x == 0] <- 0
  sub("^-", "−", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)) }
# v(): estimate; vc(): estimate [95% CI] -- x100 by default.
# Negative scale reverses the sign (e.g. to describe a gap that widens).
v  <- function(r, term, stat = "Mean", d = 1, scale = 100) f(scale * row_of(r, term, stat)$estimate, d)
vc <- function(r, term, stat = "Mean", d = 1, scale = 100) {
  x <- row_of(r, term, stat)
  b <- sort(scale * c(x$lo, x$hi))
  paste0(f(scale * x$estimate, d), " [", f(b[1], d), ", ", f(b[2], d), "]")
}
# Table cells: estimate with stars over (SE); median over [95% interval].
est_star <- function(x, d = 2, scale = 100) paste0(f(scale * x$estimate, d), sig(x$p))
se_par   <- function(x, d = 2, scale = 100) paste0("(", f(scale * x$se, d), ")")
ci_br    <- function(x, d = 2, scale = 100) {
  b <- sort(scale * c(x$lo, x$hi)); paste0("[", f(b[1], d), ", ", f(b[2], d), "]") }
npos <- function(r, term) row_of(r, term)$n_pos
nneg <- function(r, term) row_of(r, term)$n_neg
i2 <- function(r, term) round(100 * row_of(r, term)$I2)
words <- c("none", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight",
           "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen", "fourteen", "fifteen", "sixteen",
           "seventeen", "eighteen", "nineteen")
w <- function(n) format(n)   # JOB version: numbers as digits
country_name <- function(cc) unname(country_label[cc])
listc <- function(x) if (length(x) < 2) x else if (length(x) == 2) paste(x, collapse = " and ") else
  paste0(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), ", and ", x[length(x)])   # serial comma
which_c <- function(r, term, side = c("pos", "neg")) {
  side <- match.arg(side); x <- S(r, term); x <- x[!x$country %in% c("Mean", "Median"), ]
  country_name(x$country[if (side == "pos") x$lo > 0 else x$hi < 0])
}
share <- function(num, den, r = "ch") round(100 * row_of(r, num)$estimate / row_of(r, den)$estimate)
pp <- "percentile points"
# vcp(): estimate with the % sign before the interval, e.g. "3.9% [3.2, 4.6]".
vcp <- function(...) sub("^(\\S+) ", "\\1% ", vc(...))
stars_note <- "\\* p < 0.10, \\*\\* p < 0.05, \\*\\*\\* p < 0.01."

N_total <- sum(descr$n)
fmtN <- function(n) format(n, big.mark = ",")

fig <- function(p, name, width = 6.5, height = 4) {
  save_figure(p, name, fig_dir, width, height)
  knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, paste0(name, if (latex) ".pdf" else ".png")), dpi = if (latex) NA else if (knitr::pandoc_to("docx")) 300 else 110)
}
```

# Appendix {.unnumbered}

*Returns to non-cognitive skills: How much is paid through education?*

This appendix accompanies the study. Section A reports the sample construction (Table A1); Section B the total, indirect and direct effects for every country, for log hourly wages in the 12 main countries and for the earnings decile in the 19 countries of the decile sample (Tables A2–A5); Section C the skill × job-demand interactions under 3 demand measures and the sensitivity of the mediation estimates to the occupation and sector block (Tables A6 and A7); Section D the robustness checks summarized in the study (Figures A1 and A2) and the indirect effect through industry split by industry (Figure A3); Section E the indirect effect through industry by sector, without the education industry and with 2-digit occupations (Table A8), the direct effects by sector (Table A9), the tests of homogeneity across countries (Table A10), the sizes of the groups compared (Table A11), and the education term of each country against the wage differential of its education industry (Figure A4). Significance marks (\* p < 0.10, \*\* p < 0.05, \*\*\* p < 0.01) and all definitions follow the study.

# A. Sample construction

```{r}
#| label: parts
parts_all <- c(total = "Total effect", education = "Education", cognitive = "Cognitive skills",
               experience = "Experience and tenure", job_sorting = "Occupation and sector",
               industry = "Industry", tasks = "Tasks", direct = "Direct effect")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s01
#| tbl-cap: "Sample construction"
stages <- c(all = "Records in the 12 public-use files",
            age = "Aged 25–54",
            employee = "Currently employed as an employee",
            wage = "Positive hourly earnings and survey weight",
            skills = "Valid gender, education, personality scores, and plausible values",
            tasks = "Complete responses to the 9 task items",
            job = "Valid occupation group, workplace sector, and establishment size",
            final = "After the wage-quality rules (analysis sample)")
notes_flow <- "*Notes:* Each row applies one further condition to the row above. Wage-quality rules: the weighted bottom and top 1% of hourly earnings and values below 1/20 or above 20 times the weighted country median are dropped. Unweighted counts."
ltable(data.frame(unname(stages), fmtN(colSums(flow[, names(stages)])),
                  fmtN(sapply(names(stages), function(s) min(flow[[s]]))),

       header = c("Stage", "Total", "Smallest\ncountry", "Largest\ncountry"), align = "lrrr",
       space_before = length(stages), notes = notes_flow)

# B. Country-level estimates

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s07
#| tbl-cap: "Country-specific mediation estimates: total effect and direct effect of each non-cognitive skill (%, 95% intervals)"
spec_cols <- c(M0 = "A. Total effect", M4 = "B. Direct effect (net of all 6 blocks)")
ord_rows <- c(countries[order(country_name(countries))], "Mean")
ret_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(spec_cols), function(m) {
  x <- country_and_summary(res$seq, paste0(trait_names, "|", m))
  t(sapply(ord_rows, function(cc) c(if (cc %in% countries) country_name(cc) else cc,
    sapply(trait_names, function(tr) { y <- x[x$country == cc & x$term == paste0(tr, "|", m), ]
      paste0(f(100 * y$estimate), " ", ci_br(y, 1)) })))) }))
notes_ar <- paste("*Notes:* Total effect (regression with the baseline controls and the 5 non-cognitive skills) and",
  "direct effect (net of education, cognitive skills, experience and tenure, occupation and sector, industry, and tasks) per SD of each",
  "skill, from mediate (Tingley et al. 2014) with the mean of the 10 plausible values of literacy; 95%",
  "quasi-Bayesian intervals.")
ltable(ret_rows, header = c("", trait_label), align = "lccccc", long = TRUE,
       panels = setNames(c(1, 14), spec_cols),
       space_before = 13, tabcolsep = 4, notes = notes_ar)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s08
#| tbl-cap: "Causal mediation estimates by country: total effect, indirect effects through each block, and direct effect (%, standard errors in parentheses)"
ord13 <- c(countries[order(country_name(countries))], "Mean")
dec_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(trait_names, function(tr) {
  x <- country_and_summary(res$ch, paste0("mean|", tr, "|", names(parts_all)))
  t(sapply(ord13, function(cc) c(if (cc %in% countries) country_name(cc) else cc,
    sapply(names(parts_all), function(pt) { y <- x[x$country == cc & x$term == paste0("mean|", tr, "|", pt), ]
      paste0(f(100 * y$estimate, 2), " ", se_par(y)) })))) }))
notes_ac <- paste("*Notes:* Average indirect effect through each block of mediators and average direct effect from",
  "mediate (Tingley et al. 2014), mean of the 10 plausible values of literacy; they add up to the total",
  "effect. Standard errors are the standard deviation of the quasi-Bayesian draws; the mean row averages the 12 countries.")
ltable(dec_rows, header = c("", "Total\neffect", "Education", "Cognitive\nskills",
                            "Experience\nand tenure", "Occupation\nand sector", "Industry", "Tasks", "Direct\neffect"),
       align = "lcccccccc", long = TRUE,
       groups = list(list(list(label = "Indirect effect through", from = 3, to = 8))),
       panels = setNames(seq(1, by = 13, length.out = 5), trait_label),
       space_before = seq(13, by = 13, length.out = 5), tabcolsep = 2, notes = notes_ac)
```

# C. Job-demand interactions and the occupation block

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s05
#| tbl-cap: "Wage-regression interactions between matched skills and job demands under 3 demand measures (%)"
pairs <- paste(trait_names, c("influence", "organisation", "learning", "pressure", "cooperation"), sep = ":")
pr_rows <- c(pairs, "matched_mean", "mismatched_mean", "match_premium")
pr_lab <- c(paste(trait_label, "×", tolower(matched_task_label[trait_names])),
            "Mean of matched interactions", "Mean of mismatched interactions", "Match premium")
pr_grid <- function(fun) cbind(pr_lab, sapply(c("A", "C", "B", "A0", "B0"), function(r)
  sapply(pr_rows, function(t) fun(row_of(r, t)))))
notes_pairs <- paste("*Notes:* Interaction between each non-cognitive skill and the demand for its matched task,",
  "mean of countries with standard errors in parentheses. A: co-worker demand in two-digit",
  "occupation cells with two-digit occupation fixed effects (7 countries). C: co-worker demand",
  "in broad job cells. B: the respondent's own report. Job controls: experience and tenure, occupation group, sector,",
  "establishment size, and industry (two-digit occupations for A). The match premium is the mean of the 5",
  "matched interactions minus the mean of the 20 mismatched ones. Co-worker cells need at least 15",
  "respondents; broad job cells fall back from occupation × sector × establishment size to occupation × sector and then to occupation.",
  stars_note)
ltable(pr_grid(est_star), sub = pr_grid(se_par),
       header = c("", "Co-worker,\ntwo-digit (A)", "Co-worker,\nbroad cell (C)", "Own\nreport (B)",
                  "Co-worker,\ntwo-digit (A)", "Own\nreport (B)"),
       align = "lccccc", space_before = 6,
       groups = list(list(list(label = "With job controls", from = 2, to = 4),
                          list(label = "Without job controls", from = 5, to = 6))),
       notes = notes_pairs)
```

`r table_notes(notes_pairs)`

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s06
#| tbl-cap: "Causal mediation estimates under alternative occupation and sector blocks (%)"
sens_specs <- c("ch", "sup", "broadA", "occ2")
sens_grid <- function(fun, part) do.call(rbind, lapply(trait_names, function(tr)
  c(trait_label[[tr]], sapply(sens_specs, function(r) {
    x <- country_and_summary(res[[r]], paste0("mean|", tr, "|", part)); fun(x[x$country == "Mean", ]) }))))
notes_sens <- paste("*Notes:* Indirect effect through the occupation and sector block and direct effect from mediate, with all 6 blocks in the model;",
  "mean of countries with quasi-Bayesian standard errors in parentheses. Main: occupation and sector block with 4 occupation groups, sector, and",
  "establishment size (12 countries). With supervision: adds an indicator for supervising",
  "other employees to the block. The 7 countries are Chile, Czechia, France, Italy, Latvia, Poland,",
  "and Spain, with the 4 occupation groups or with two-digit ISCO-08 occupations in the block.")
ltable(rbind(sens_grid(function(x) f(100 * x$estimate, 2), "job_sorting"),
             sens_grid(function(x) f(100 * x$estimate, 2), "direct")),
       sub = rbind(sens_grid(se_par, "job_sorting"), sens_grid(se_par, "direct")),
       header = c("", "Main", "With\nsupervision", "Occupation\ngroups", "Two-digit\noccupations"),
       align = "lcccc",
       groups = list(list(list(label = "12 countries", from = 2, to = 3),
                          list(label = "7 countries", from = 4, to = 5))),
       panels = c("A. Indirect effect through occupation and sector" = 1, "B. Direct effect" = 6),
       notes = notes_sens)

# D. Robustness

```{r}
#| label: sens-data
oriv <- lapply(R("rob_oriv"), function(r) transform(r, term = paste0("mean|", term)))
B_c <- names(oriv)
checks <- list(
  "Main estimate" = res$m1,
  "Numeracy instead of literacy" = R("rob_numeracy"),
  "Literacy and numeracy" = R("rob_both"),
  "Untrimmed earnings" = R("rob_untrimmed"),
  "Earnings without bonuses" = R("rob_nobonus"),
  "Without Poland" = res$m1[setdiff(countries, "POL")],
  "Six-item countries, uncorrected" = res$m1[B_c],
  "Six-item countries, split-half IV" = oriv)
rob_m <- function(lab, tr) { x <- country_and_summary(checks[[lab]], paste0("mean|", tr)); x[x$country == "Mean", ] }
rv_ <- function(lab, tr) f(100 * rob_m(lab, tr)$estimate)
loo <- sapply(countries, function(cc) { p <- country_and_summary(res$m1[setdiff(countries, cc)], paste0("mean|", trait_names))
  p <- p[p$country == "Mean", ]; 100 * p$estimate[match(paste0("mean|", trait_names), p$term)] })
main_m1 <- sapply(trait_names, function(tr) 100 * rob_m("Main estimate", tr)$estimate)
loo_dev <- max(abs(loo - main_m1))
re <- pool_terms(res$m1); re <- re[match(paste0("mean|", trait_names), re$term), ]
re_dev <- max(abs(100 * re$pooled - main_m1))
bench_w <- row_of("rv1", "bench_wage")$estimate
bench_t <- max(sapply(trait_names, function(tr) row_of("rv1", paste0("bench_trait|", tr))$estimate))
rv_min <- min(sapply(trait_names, function(tr) row_of("rv1", paste0("rv|", tr))$estimate))
rv_max <- max(sapply(trait_names, function(tr) row_of("rv1", paste0("rv|", tr))$estimate))
sup_ <- function(tr, pt) f(100 * row_of("sup", paste0("mean|", tr, "|", pt))$estimate, 2)
occ_ <- function(r, tr, pt) { x <- country_and_summary(res[[r]], paste0("mean|", tr, "|", pt)); f(100 * x$estimate[x$country == "Mean"], 2) }
occ_num <- function(r, tr, pt) { x <- country_and_summary(res[[r]], paste0("mean|", tr, "|", pt)); 100 * x$estimate[x$country == "Mean"] }
occ_rem_dev <- max(sapply(trait_names, function(tr) abs(occ_num("occ2", tr, "direct") - occ_num("broadA", tr, "direct"))))
```

The returns net of education and cognitive skills change little under alternative specifications: numeracy instead of literacy, literacy and numeracy together, untrimmed earnings, earnings without bonuses, and the sample without Poland (@fig-s2). No single country moves a mean return by more than `r f(loo_dev, 1)`%, and a random-effects pooling of the 12 countries differs from the simple mean by at most `r f(re_dev, 1)`%. Measurement error in the 3-item scores works in the other direction: in the 7 countries with 6-item scales, a split-half instrumental-variable correction [@gillen2019] raises the extraversion return from `r rv_("Six-item countries, uncorrected", "EXTR")` to `r rv_("Six-item countries, split-half IV", "EXTR")`%.

@fig-s3 reports the robustness values of @cinelli2020. To reduce a direct effect to zero, an unobserved confounder would have to explain between `r f(100 * rv_min, 1)`% and `r f(100 * rv_max, 1)`% of the residual variance of log wages, and the same share of the residual variance of the non-cognitive skill. For comparison, parental education explains `r f(100 * bench_w, 1)`% of the residual variance of wages and at most `r f(100 * bench_t, 1)`% of the residual variance of a non-cognitive skill.

The second 3-item half is reconstructed from the published 3-item and 6-item scores under the assumption of parallel items, so this check is approximate."
fig(fig_robustness_checks(checks, unit = "%"), "fig8_robustness", 6.5, 3.3)

Circles are countries; the diamond is the mean of countries with its 95% interval. The shaded area extends to the larger of the two parental-education benchmarks (mean of countries)."

# E. Industry, sector and country

```{r}
#| label: sector-data
grp_grid <- function(rows, fun, pre, part) do.call(rbind, lapply(rows, function(r)
  c(r[1], sapply(trait_names, function(tr) fun(row_of(paste0(pre, r[2]), paste0(r[3], "|", tr, "|", part)))))))
k_occ <- length(res$e_occ2); k_occ_d <- length(res$d_e_occ2)
rng <- function(x) paste(format(min(x), big.mark = ","), "to", format(max(x), big.mark = ","))
```

Table A8 reports the indirect effect through industry in groups of employees, and Table A9 the direct effects by sector. Table A10 reports the homogeneity test of @cochran1954 for the wage differential of each industry and for the effect of each skill on working in it, with the education industry shown separately. Table A11 gives the number of employees in each group by country. Figure A4 compares, country by country, the education term with the wage differential.

```{r}

#| label: tbl-s13
#| tbl-cap: "Homogeneity across countries of industry wage differentials and of the sorting of non-cognitive skills into industries"
of <- function(a, n, unit = "industries") paste(a, "of", n, unit)
q_cell <- function(h, term) { q <- h[h$term == term, ]
  paste0("Q = ", formatC(q$Q, format = "f", digits = 1), ", p ", if (q$p < 0.001) "< 0.001" else paste("=", formatC(q$p, format = "f", digits = 3))) }
q_edu <- list(c("Wage differential of the education industry", "premium|P"),
  c("Education term: open-mindedness", "OPEM|P|contrib"), c("Education term: agreeableness", "AGRE|P|contrib"),
  c("Sorting into education: open-mindedness", "OPEM|P|sorting"), c("Sorting into education: agreeableness", "AGRE|P|sorting"))
q_body <- rbind(
  c("Industry wage differential", of(hc$premium, length(hc$industries)), of(hc_d$premium, length(hc_d$industries))),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(trait_names, function(tr) c(paste("Sorting into the industry:", tolower(trait_label[[tr]])),
    of(hc$sorting[[tr]], length(hc$industries)), of(hc_d$sorting[[tr]], length(hc_d$industries))))),
  c("Sorting into the industry: all 5 skills", of(sum(hc$sorting), 5 * length(hc$industries), "pairs"), of(sum(hc_d$sorting), 5 * length(hc_d$industries), "pairs")),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(q_edu, function(r) c(r[1], q_cell(hom_edu, r[2]), q_cell(hom_edu_d, r[2])))))
notes_q <- paste("*Notes:* Q statistic of Cochran (1954) for the equality of a quantity across countries, from the country estimates and their standard errors",
  "(replicate weights and the 10 plausible values); under equality, Q follows a chi-square distribution with the number of countries minus 1 degrees of freedom",
  paste0("(", hom_edu$df[1], " and ", hom_edu_d$df[1], ")."),
  "Columns are the 2 samples. Panel A: of the industries tested in a sample (ISIC Rev. 4 sections with at least 2% of employment on average and an estimate in every country),",
  "the number in which equality across the countries of that sample is rejected at the 5% level; the last row counts skill–industry pairs. The counts are descriptive and are not adjusted for the number of tests.",
  "The wage differential of an industry is measured against the average job of workers with comparable education, cognitive skills,",
  "experience and tenure, occupation, sector and tasks; sorting is the effect of the skill on the probability of working in the industry.",
  "The education term is the sorting into the education industry (section P) times its wage differential.")
ltable(q_body, header = c("", sprintf("Log hourly wages,\n%d countries", K), sprintf("Earnings decile,\n%d countries", K_d)), align = "lcc",

# F. Returns by education and literacy

Table A12 reports the returns to each non-cognitive skill estimated in separate samples and the linear interactions of each skill with tertiary education and literacy. They accompany the forest estimates of Table 3.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s15
#| tbl-cap: "Return to each non-cognitive skill by education and literacy: separate samples and linear interactions"
hx_rows <- list(c("Tertiary graduates", "ss", "graduates|%s"), c("Non-graduates", "ss", "non_graduates|%s"),
  c("Graduates minus non-graduates", "ss", "diff_edu|%s"), c("Top third of literacy", "ss", "lit_top|%s"),
  c("Bottom third of literacy", "ss", "lit_bottom|%s"), c("Top minus bottom third", "ss", "diff_lit|%s"),
  c("Skill × tertiary education", "sc", "%s|x_tertiary"), c("Skill × literacy (per SD)", "sc", "%s|x_literacy"))
hx_sets <- c("", "d_%s12", "d_%s7")
hx_grid <- function(fun) do.call(rbind, lapply(hx_sets, function(st) do.call(rbind, lapply(hx_rows, function(r) {
  key <- if (st == "") r[2] else sprintf(st, r[2])
  c(r[1], sapply(trait_names, function(tr) fun(row_of(key, sprintf(r[3], tr))))) }))))
notes_hx <- paste("*Notes:* Wage equation with the 5 skills, the baseline controls, education and the literacy quadratic.",
  "The first 6 rows of each panel estimate it in separate samples: tertiary graduates and non-graduates, and the top and bottom thirds of literacy within each country;",
  "the stars of the 2 difference rows test whether the returns in the 2 samples are equal.",
  "The last 2 rows are the coefficients on the interactions of each skill with tertiary education and with literacy, with all 10 interactions in one equation.",
  "Mean of countries per SD of the skill, with standard errors from the replicate weights and the 10 plausible values in parentheses.", stars_note,
  "Panel A in %; Panels B and C in percentile points of the national earnings distribution.")
ltable(hx_grid(est_star), sub = hx_grid(se_par),
       header = c("", "Extraversion", "Conscien-\ntiousness", "Open-\nmindedness", "Emotional\nstability", "Agreeable-\nness"), align = "lccccc",
       panels = setNames(1 + length(hx_rows) * 0:2, c(sprintf("A. Log hourly wages, %d countries", K),
                         sprintf("B. Earnings decile, the same %d countries", K), sprintf("C. Earnings decile, %d further countries", K_d - K))),
       tabcolsep = 4, notes = notes_hx)
